headline: GOLD X2 MINING DRILLS 172.0m AT 0.96 g/t Au IN MOSS INFILL PROGRAM — UPDATED RESOURCE DUE Q1 2027
snippet: Gold X2 Mining (TSXV: AUXX) reported a combined 172.0 metres at 0.96 g/t Au from infill drilling at its Moss gold project in Ontario, headlined by hole MMD-26-430 in the Main Zone. Nine holes across the Main and Southwest Zones are expected to have significant impact on the updated mineral resource estimate targeted for Q1 2027.

headline: McKINSEY: GOLD DRIVES MINING INDUSTRY TO RECORD EBITDA IN 2026 — BUT PRODUCTIVITY GROWTH STALLS
snippet: McKinsey's 2026 Global Materials Perspective finds that gold prices rose 45% year-on-year, pushing the yellow metal past steel and thermal coal to claim the largest share of the industry's EBITDA pool for the first time. The report also flags a warning: despite record financial returns, the industry's operational productivity has stalled, raising long-term questions about cost control as reserves get harder to find.

headline: SSR MINING TO ACQUIRE ROXMORE RESOURCES FOR C$712M TOTAL — CONVERSE GOLD PROJECT ADDS 2.2M OZ NEXT TO MARIGOLD
snippet: SSR Mining agreed to acquire Roxmore Resources in an all-cash deal worth approximately C$712 million on a fully diluted basis, including a spinco that Roxmore shareholders will receive alongside $6.75 cash per share — a 27% premium. The main asset, the Converse Gold Project in Nevada, sits just 6 km from SSR's existing Marigold mine and hosts 2.2 million indicated ounces at 0.65 g/t, with first production targeted for 2033.

headline: LONG-TERM URANIUM PRICE TOPS $96.50/LB — SURPASSES 2007 PEAK FOR FIRST TIME IN NEARLY TWO DECADES
snippet: The long-term uranium contract price closed September 2026 at $96.50 per pound of U3O8, the highest reading in a series dating back to 1996 and a milestone that surpasses the famous 2007 bull-market peak. Spot uranium ended September at $89.63/lb — up 8.5% year-over-year — while Kazatomprom's 10% production guidance cut continues to squeeze a market where utilities are increasingly locking in term supply.

headline: LUCA MINING CLOSES C$211M SUBSCRIPTION RECEIPT FINANCING TO ACQUIRE CAPSTONE'S COZAMIN COPPER-SILVER MINE
snippet: Luca Mining completed a C$211 million bought-deal private placement of subscription receipts, securing the funding needed to close its $385 million acquisition of Capstone Copper's Cozamin mine in Zacatecas, Mexico. The deal, first announced September 21, is expected to more than double Luca's 2027 production profile; operating cash flow is projected at $223 million next year, up from $37 million in 2025.

headline: CRITICAL METALS JUMPS 4% AS TRUMP ORDERS GREENLAND MINERAL SURVEYS — USA RARE EARTH FALLS 3%, MP SLIPS 2%
snippet: Critical Metals (CRML) was the rare winner in an otherwise weak rare earth sector session after President Trump announced large-scale mineral exploration is set to begin in Greenland — CRML is the only major US-listed rare earth developer with a Greenland project. Meanwhile USA Rare Earth fell 3% and MP Materials slipped 2%, weighed down by continued US-China diplomatic warming that chips away at the domestic supply chain investment thesis.

headline: GOLD REBOUNDS NEAR $4,150 AS MARKETS PIVOT TO OCT 27-28 FOMC — YIELDS DIP DESPITE HOTTER PPI DATA
snippet: Gold steadied in the $4,145–$4,180 range as the market digested back-to-back CPI and PPI beats and attention shifted to the October 27-28 Federal Open Market Committee meeting. Treasury yields slipped slightly despite the hot PPI print, easing pressure on the dollar and offering gold a near-term floor, with TD Securities and other dealers projecting a holding pattern in the $4,000–$4,100 range pending the Fed's next move.

headline: VanECK: GOLD MINERS SUSTAINING STRENGTH AS COSTS STABILIZE — AISC GROWTH SLOWING WHILE GOLD PRICE HOLDS
snippet: VanEck's Imaru Casanova makes the case that gold miners can sustain earnings strength in a structurally higher gold price environment, citing stabilizing all-in sustaining costs and a gold price still well above the mid-$3,000s where margins compress. The analysis pushes back against market skepticism that high gold prices are already fully priced into producer equities.

headline: COPPER WEEKLY: THREE-DAY SLIDE TO $6.53/LB — MACRO NOISE OVERSHADOWING TIGHT PHYSICAL SUPPLY
snippet: LME copper entered the week at record territory near $14,800 per tonne before retreating for three straight sessions to $14,338/t ($6.53/lb), as hot US inflation data raised the probability of a Fed rate hike to nearly 50%. The weekly brief notes that the underlying supply structure — constrained by Chilean output risks at Centinela and El Teniente — remains bullish, and that macro-driven selloffs have been buying opportunities throughout 2026.

headline: GOLD MINERS VS BULLION: NORTHERN STAR AND CAPRICORN TEST THE VALUE ARGUMENT AT CURRENT PRICES
snippet: A Discovery Alert deep-dive on Northern Star and Capricorn Resources finds both Australian producers trading 20-23% below their January 2026 peaks even as gold holds above $4,000/oz — highlighting a disconnect that analysts attribute to cost inflation, production guidance misses, and the lingering premium markets still attach to physical metal over equity exposure. The piece examines whether current entry points justify the leverage trade over direct bullion ownership.
